messages:
deploy-bot: [ALERT] spike in 5xxs for eu-west model endpoints — aggregated error rate 12% over 2m. Autoscale attempted but backend health shows route failures.
netops-alex: seeing DNS inconsistencies across resolvers. some resolvers still resolving old eu-west IPs despite failover A change 18m ago.
oncall-julie: confirmed — our healthcheck pings to eu-west are failing and traffic didn't fully shift to us-west. Lots of curl timeouts from eu clients.
eng-sre-mike: paste dig outputs I'm seeing from a few resolvers: 
```
$ dig @8.8.8.8 api.model-eu.redwood-inference.com +short
203.0.113.12    ; OLD eu-west pool
$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.model-eu.redwood-inference.com +short
198.51.100.45   ; NEW us-west pool
$ dig +trace api.model-eu.redwood-inference.com
; <<>> DiG 9.10.6 <<>> +trace api.model-eu.redwood-inference.com
;; Received 172 bytes from 203.0.113.53#53(203.0.113.53) in 24 ms
api.model-eu.redwood-inference.com. 3600 IN A 203.0.113.12
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
redwood-inference.com. 86400 IN NS ns1.registrar.example.
```
netops-alex: looks like the authoritative A TTL is 3600 (1h) but delegation/registrar had NS records with 24h. older resolvers are honoring parent/registry caching and SOA MINs — hence the race. also some corporate resolvers apply minimum caching (https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2308) so reducing TTL now won't fix everywhere.
prod-ops-sam: tl;dr we changed A records to point to us-west, but a subset of resolvers are still returning eu-west due to cached delegation/soa info. impact: approx 10-15% of traffic still hitting degraded eu-west GPUs causing higher tail latency and 5xx ramp.
eng-sre-mike: quick troubleshooting steps I ran: 
- verified eu-west NVA/health is really unhealthy (OOM on a few GPU nodes after degradation)
- tried host-level curl from a few providers (some go to old IP, some to new)
- ran `dig +nocmd +noall +answer @ns1.registrar.example api.model-eu.redwood-inference.com` — registrar's view shows new IP.

oncall-julie: mitigation plan — immediate and short term: 
1) Add temporary TCP/HTTP health-check redirect at old eu-west IPs to respond 302 -> health page so upstream proxies will see success and not retry? (not ideal).
2) Spin up extra Dedicated capacity in us-west and increase routing weight from regional router (not DNS) to accelerate movement off eu-west.
3) Contact major DNS providers (Google Public DNS/Cloudflare) and file cache flush/clear requests — they have tools for high-priority flushes.
4) Prep postmortem items to change runbook: ensure lower parent TTLs before any planned region shift.

netops-alex: also recommend we update SOA MINIMUM to 60s for this zone and push an auth-NS change AFTER hours to avoid registry-level long cache effects. current SOA MIN shows 86400s on some caches. that's the negative caching TTL that makes NX/redirects sticky.

customer-success-chen: customers are asking for ETA — we should give conservative timeline. If we can push routing weight and spin up us-west GPUs now, can we get error rate <1% in 30-45m?

eng-sre-mike: optimistic path: with traffic steering + extra us-west capacity we cut 5xxs to ~1-2% in 25-40m. DNS-only approach would have taken hours for some resolvers.

prod-ops-sam: I'm already launching 8x new GPU nodes in us-west (reserved pool) and enabling aggressive weighting on the traffic router. Also enabling model fallback mode (safe-cpu) for non-critical routes to reduce GPU pressure.

netops-alex: actioned SOA change to 60s and decreased A record TTL to 30s on authoritative DNS (posted change to registrar). Note: registrar propagation might still respect previous NS TTL for a while.

oncall-julie: contact notes — reached out to Google DNS SRE with ticket ID G-DNS-8421 and Cloudflare incident 34567 — asking for expedited cache flush for our A records and delegation.

eng-sre-mike: small gotcha observed — some ISP resolvers treat the SOA MIN differently (as upper bound); we should record examples for postmortem. Eg: `isp-x-resolver` still returned old IP at +90m.

customer-success-chen: messaging to affected customers drafted: short apology, mitigation steps, ETA and ask for any immediate customer traffic patterns to escalate.

oncall-julie: current status update: traffic weighting + capacity increased. error rate down to 2.7% over last 5m. a subset (~6-9%) of EU clients still hitting old IPs. still chasing last-mile resolvers.

prod-ops-sam: cost note — spinning extra GPUs and higher cross-region egress will show in tonight's cost dashboard. flagging to finance for possible credit to affected customers.

eng-sre-mike: next steps for post-incident runbook changes (to assign): 
- preflight TTL plan before any planned region shift (set parent delegation TTLs low at least 48h before)
- keep an emergency IP-level redirect capability on eu pools for graceful drains
- test resolver behavior matrix (isp, cloud dns, enterprise) for TTL and SOA handling
- add automated contact workflow for major public DNS providers in playbook
- include guidance to prefer router-level weighted failover vs purely DNS-based for critical model endpoints

netops-alex: logging the SOA and delegation mismatch in the incident timeline. registrar confirmed change accepted at 1912350100.

oncall-julie: closing update in 40m — final postmortem to be written. For now: we are in recovery, 5xxs trending down, traffic shifted predominantly to us-west.

customer-success-chen: thanks team — I'll update customer threads and keep them informed about postmortem and credits. :thumbsup:
